About Block Puzzle (1010!)

Block Puzzle is a modern spatial packing and line-clearing game blending geometric polyomino aesthetics with pure 10×10 zero-gravity puzzle planning. Stripping away the gravity and countdown timers of Tetris, it grants complete freedom to strategize your moves across a 100-cell grid. Fully responsive across desktop, tablet, and mobile browsers with instant play.

Game Controls

ActionMouse / TouchscreenKeyboardDescription
Select ShapeClick hand slot / Drag shape1 / 2 / 3Select hand piece (elevated cyan border); click again to deselect
Move / PreviewHover board cell / Drag across boardWASD or ↑←↓→Move cursor and preview ghost placement shadow
Commit PlacementClick cell / Release dragSpace or EnterPlace piece at valid position and trigger clears
Cancel SelectionClick board backdropEscDeselect current hand shape
Quick RestartClick top Restart buttonRInstantly reset game in single-player mode

Core Mechanics

  • 10×10 Zero-Gravity Grid: Place shapes anywhere without gravity. Shapes cannot be rotated; adapt your grid topography to fit them.
  • Triad Batch Dealing: Shapes are dealt in sets of 3. New shapes arrive only after all 3 are played. Always plan all three steps!
  • Row & Column Clears: Completely filling any horizontal row or vertical column detonates it instantly, reclaiming space.
  • Combo Multipliers: Clearing multiple lines simultaneously (2–5 lines) or maintaining consecutive clears scales score exponentially!

Scoring Matrix

Clear TypeLines ClearedBase ScoreCombo Formula
Single Clear1 Line100 ptsBase × (1 + 0.5 × (Combo - 1))
Double / Cross Clear2 Lines360 ptsHigh efficiency core tactic
Triple Clear3 Lines800 ptsTactical burst
Quad Clear4 Lines1,600 ptsScreen-clearing laser blast
Perfect All-ClearWipe 100% board+1,500 BonusBoard fully emptied

Master Creed

"Preserve the 3×3 Sanctuary, Plan the Entire Triad, Cascade Continuous Clears, Step by Prudent Step." Always hold a pristine 3×3 void to survive sudden giant square spawns.

Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ)

Can I rotate shapes?

No. Fixed orientation is the core rule of Block Puzzle. Sculpt your board to fit incoming pieces rather than trying to rotate them.

Does touch dragging block the view?

Not at all! Our smart offset algorithm renders dragged pieces comfortably above your fingertip. You can also tap a hand piece and then tap a board cell to place it without dragging.

How does multiplayer PK work?

Players share identical pseudo-random shape sequences in real time, competing strictly on spatial efficiency and combo execution.

game.classic2048.seo_desc:
About Classic 2048 (Number Tile Sliding Puzzle)

Classic 2048 is a world-renowned sliding-tile puzzle game that became a global phenomenon in 2014. Created by Gabriele Cirulli, it features an elegant 4×4 grid where numbers combine by powers of two. With pure spatial planning and zero time pressure, every swipe slides all tiles across the grid until identical numbers collide and merge into double their value: 2, 4, 8, 16... all the way to the golden 2048 tile! Smooth, lightning-fast, and universally engaging on both touchscreens and desktop keyboards.

Controls & Keyboard Shortcuts Guide

Action Touch Gesture (Phone / Tablet) Keyboard Key Description
Slide Left Swipe Left across the board A or ← Arrow Slides all tiles leftward; identical colliding tiles merge
Slide Right Swipe Right across the board D or → Arrow Slides all tiles rightward; identical colliding tiles merge
Slide Up Swipe Up across the board W or ↑ Arrow Slides all tiles upward; identical colliding tiles merge
Slide Down Swipe Down across the board S or ↓ Arrow Slides all tiles downward; identical colliding tiles merge
Undo Move Tap Undo button on top toolbar U or Ctrl + Z Rolls back the last swipe in single-player practice mode
Restart Board Tap Restart button R Clears the 4×4 board to start fresh with zero score

Tile Mechanics & Spawn Rules

  • Collision & Doubling: When two tiles with identical values collide, they merge into one with double the value (e.g., 2+2=4, 4+4=8, 1024+1024=2048).
  • One Merge Per Slide: A row with [2, 2, 2, 2] sliding left becomes [4, 4, 0, 0], never jumping directly to an 8 in one swipe.
  • New Tile Spawns: Every valid move generates a new tile in an empty cell: 90% chance of a 2, and 10% chance of a 4.
  • Game Over Condition: The game ends when all 16 cells are full and no adjacent tiles can merge horizontally or vertically.

Three Golden Rules for 2048 Mastery

  • Rule 1: Lock the Corner (The King's Throne): Never let your highest tile wander in the center. Pick one corner (bottom-right is classic) and anchor your biggest tile there permanently.
  • Rule 2: Snake Order (From Largest to Smallest): Arrange remaining numbers in descending snake-like order (e.g., bottom row: 1024, 512, 256, 128). When the tail merges, it triggers a zipper cascade!
  • Rule 3: Seal the Opposite Direction: If your king tile is anchored in the bottom-right, NEVER press Up! Use only Left, Right, and Down to prevent pulling your high tile away from the bottom wall.

Real-Time Speed PK Battles

  • Identical Random Seeds: Both opponents play with the exact same spawn sequence for 100% competitive fairness.
  • First to 2048 Wins: Race to create the 2048 tile first, or outlast your rival if their board fills up first!
game.codebreaker.seo_desc:
About Codebreaker (Bulls and Cows / 1A2B)

Codebreaker is a legendary deduction and cryptanalysis puzzle rooted in the historic 19th-century game Bulls and Cows and the commercial board classic Mastermind. Your objective is to crack a secret unique-digit code generated by the system within a limited number of trials. After each deduction attempt, the engine provides exact feedback in the form of A (Bulls: correct digit and correct position) and B (Cows: correct digit but wrong position). Featuring client-side instant execution, customizable difficulty, and real-time multiplayer speed duels!

Keybindings & Control Guide

Action Keyboard Key Mouse / Touch Description
Input Digit 0 - 9 Tap virtual number pad Fills current empty slot (duplicate digits are prevented)
Backspace Backspace / Delete Tap red erase button Removes the most recent digit entered
Clear All Esc Double tap clear button Resets the entire current input row
Submit Guess Enter Tap glowing Submit button Validates guess and reveals ?A?B feedback instantly
Deduction Scratchpad - Tap scratchpad circles Cycle 3 states: Default Neutral → Strikethrough Cross → Green Confirmed

Core Mechanics: The 1A2B Clue Algebra

Every time you submit a guess, the evaluation engine scores your guess against the secret code with two metrics:

  • A (Bulls / Exact Matches): The digit exists in the secret code AND is in the exact right position.
  • B (Cows / Permutation Matches): The digit exists in the secret code, but is located in a different position.
  • Important: Feedback pegs provide aggregate counts only, never pinpointing which individual slots matched! For example, if the secret is 1234 and you guess 1543, you receive 1A2B (digit 1 is at slot 1 = 1A; digits 3 and 4 exist but are displaced = 2B; digit 5 is completely absent).

Pro Solving Strategies & Information Theory

  1. The Dual-Probing Opener (0123 / 4567): Guessing two completely disjoint sets tests 8 out of the 10 available digits in just 2 turns. Summing the total clues (A+B) reveals whether the remaining unprobed digits (8 and 9) are in the code, collapsing the search space from 5,040 to under 40 candidates!
  2. Zero-Feedback Elimination Jackpot: Receiving 0A0B is the biggest tactical breakthrough in the game. It completely eliminates 4 digits at once. The candidate pool shrinks from 5,040 to P(6,4) = 360, eliminating 92.86% of all possibilities in a single stroke!
  3. Single-Variable Substitution: When testing confirmed digit candidates, alter only one slot at a time. If total clues increase, the new digit is guaranteed present. If total clues decrease, the replaced digit was part of the secret code.

Real-Time Multiplayer Speed PK

  • Identical Secret Code: Both contenders race against the exact same seed, ensuring pure competitive parity.
  • Live Progress Telemetry: Keep an eye on your opponent's attempt count, highest achieved 'A' count, and cadence to pace your analytical moves against intuition.
  • First to 4A0B Wins: Break the code in fewer attempts or faster time to claim victory and leaderboard trophies.

Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ)

Can a guess ever produce 3A1B?

Never! In a 4-digit code, if 3 digits are in their exact correct positions (3A), the remaining 4th digit has only one vacant position. It is either the correct digit (giving 4A0B), or an incorrect digit (giving 3A0B). It can never be displaced in another position, making 3A1B a mathematical impossibility.

Where can I study advanced Knuth Five-Guess algorithms and candidate matrices?

Explore our definitive masterclass guide: 《Codebreaker Deep Strategy Guide & Information Theory Algorithm Book》, featuring Donald Knuth's Minimax tree analysis, 14 feedback partition theorems, and candidate reduction tables!

About Connect Colors (Numberlink / Flow Puzzle)

Connect Colors (widely known internationally as Numberlink or Flow Free) is a beloved spatial logic puzzle. Your mission is simple yet delightfully challenging: connect matching pairs of colored and numbered dots by drawing continuous pipes between them. Pipes cannot cross or overlap, and every single square on the board must be fully covered (100% board coverage)! Smooth, intuitive touch drag and keyboard controls make it ideal for puzzle lovers of all ages.

Controls & Keyboard Shortcuts Guide

Action Mouse Interaction Touch Gesture (Phone / Tablet) Keyboard Key Description
Draw Pipe Click and drag from dot to dot Press dot and drag finger to target - Draws a colored pipe connecting matching dots
Retract / Trim Drag backward along pipe path Slide finger backward along line - Shortens or clears an errant pipe segment
AI Hint Click top lightbulb 💡 button Tap hint lightbulb icon H Key Reveals and connects one correct pipe in solo mode
Restart Board Click restart button Tap restart icon R Key Clears all drawn pipes to start the board fresh

The Two Golden Rules of Connect Colors

  • Connect Pairs with No Crossings: Connect every pair of matching colored dots. Pipes cannot cross or overlap. If you drag a new pipe across an existing one, the old pipe breaks!
  • 100% Full Board Coverage: Every single square on the grid must be covered by a pipe. If all pairs are connected but empty squares remain, pulsing stars ✦ will highlight the unfilled spots!

Four Essential Solving Tactics

  • Hug the Outer Border First: Dots near the outer walls and corners usually have only one viable path. Trace the boundary first to leave open space in the center.
  • Connect Short Distances Early: Pair up adjacent dots with tight paths so they don't block longer routes.
  • Respect Narrow Bottlenecks: When two zones are separated by a one-cell corridor, only the pipe that truly needs to cross should use it.
  • Snake Winding for 100% Coverage: If all dots are connected but a few empty squares remain, take a straight pipe nearby and wind it in an S-curve to fill the gaps!

Real-Time Speed PK Arena

  • Fair Identical Seed: Both players solve the exact same board setup simultaneously.
  • First to 100% Wins: Watch your rival's live progress percentage in the top HUD and race to complete all pipes!

game.drop2048.seo_desc:
About Drop 2048 (Tetris 2048)

Drop 2048 is an incredibly addictive and innovative puzzle game that brilliantly fuses the falling-block mechanics of Tetris with the number-merging logic of classic 2048. Unlike traditional 2048 which allows for slow, deliberate planning, Drop 2048 demands rapid spatial awareness and split-second reflexes as numbers continuously rain from above. Play free online directly in your browser and experience the ultimate satisfaction of explosive number chains!

Core Mechanics & Merging Rules

As the game begins, blocks featuring base numbers (like 2, 4, or 8) will continuously fall from the top of the grid. Your objective is to move these blocks left or right and drop them into the optimal columns:

  • Same-Number Merging: When a falling block lands on or adjacent to another block with the exact same number, they instantly fuse into a single block with double the value (e.g., two 8s merge into a 16; two 1024s merge into a 2048).
  • Chain Reactions (Combos): This is where the game shines. A successful merge may cause the blocks stacked above it to fall further down. If they land on matching numbers, it triggers a cascading chain reaction of automatic merges!
  • Survival Rule: If your columns of blocks stack too high and cross the danger line at the top of the board, it's Game Over.

Advanced Strategies for High Scores

To dominate the global leaderboards, you cannot just drop blocks randomly. You must master the \"Number Pyramid\" stacking strategy:

  • Keep Big Numbers at the Bottom: Always strive to keep your highest synthesized numbers (like 512 or 1024) buried at the very bottom of the grid. If a small number gets trapped beneath a large number, that column becomes dead weight.
  • Staircase Layout: Arrange your numbers in a descending sequential order (e.g., 64, 32, 16, 8) either vertically or horizontally. When a new 8 drops in, it will trigger a satisfying domino effect: 8->16->32->64->128!
  • Look Ahead: Never just watch the current falling block. Always keep an eye on the \"Next Block\" preview to leave a strategic gap for upcoming numbers.

X-Game's Exclusive Multiplayer Battles

Tired of just beating your own high score? We have introduced a revolutionary Real-Time Multiplayer PvP Mode:

  • Face off against your friends or players worldwide in a shared lobby.
  • Garbage Attacks: When you execute massive Chain Reactions or merge exceptionally high numbers, you send un-mergeable \"Garbage Blocks\" straight to your opponent's board, pushing their stack closer to the ceiling of death.
  • It's a fast-paced test of offensive combos and desperate defensive survival. Only the fastest mind wins!

Ready to brave the falling numbers? Hit play and push your merging limits to the max!

FAQ

Is Drop 2048 free to play?

Yes, Drop 2048 is 100% free on Puzzle PK. There are no downloads, no installations, and no in-game purchases required to play. Open the game in any modern browser and the blocks start falling within seconds.

Can I play Drop 2048 on my phone?

Definitely. Drop 2048 is fully playable on mobile and tablet browsers with touch controls designed for one-handed play, and it works just as well on desktop with keyboard controls. You can squeeze in a quick round anywhere, whether you are waiting for the bus or relaxing at home.

How does the Drop 2048 PK mode work?

The PK mode is a real-time 1v1 battle on separate boards. You and your opponent build at the same time, and the winner is the player who survives longer and finishes with the higher score. Every big merge or chain reaction sends garbage blocks to your rival's board, so offense and defense matter equally in every match.

What is a good score in Drop 2048?

Merging a 2048 block in a single run is a solid milestone for casual players, while experienced players regularly push on to 4096. Since your score mainly comes from merges and chain reactions, a longer survival time with more combos naturally means a bigger number. In PK mode, absolute scores matter less than finishing ahead of your opponent.

What are the best beginner tips for Drop 2048?

Keep your columns roughly even in height so no single column races toward the danger line, and always prefer the drop that completes a merge over one that simply adds height. When garbage blocks land in PK, don't panic: keep making small merges to free space underneath, and treat every match as practice for your recovery skills.

Can I play Drop 2048 with friends?

Yes. Open the PK lobby, create a room, and share the room code with your friends. They can join instantly from a phone, tablet, or computer, and the match runs in real time, making Drop 2048 a perfect quick duel for friend groups.

game.gomoku.seo_desc:
Objective & Rules of Classic Gomoku (Five in a Row)

Gomoku (Five in a Row) is an ancient, world-renowned dual-strategy board game originating in East Asia. Played on a standard 15×15 grid (225 intersections), Black plays first, followed by White in alternating turns. The victory condition is mathematically pure and strategically profound:

  • Five-in-a-Row Victory: The first player to form an unbroken chain of five stones of their color horizontally, vertically, or diagonally wins immediately.
  • Standard Gomoku Rules (Free Style): Puzzle PK uses standard freestyle Gomoku rules without restrictive fouls (no overline bans; forming 6 or more contiguous stones also counts as a valid win).
  • Deterministic Zero-Sum Contest: Gomoku features zero hidden information and zero RNG luck; outcomes are determined entirely by positional foresight, initiative control, and tactical calculation.

Complete Controls & Keyboard Shortcuts Guide

Engineered for fluid, zero-latency precision on desktop mice, keyboards, and mobile touch devices alike:

ActionKey / GestureDescription
Place StoneLeft-click / Tap intersectionPlay a stone on any vacant intersection; features translucent hover preview to avoid slips
AI Move HintKeyboard H Key / Toolbar 💡 ButtonInvokes the onboard game-tree AI to highlight the highest win-rate move on the board
Quick RestartKeyboard R KeyInstantly clears the board and restarts a fresh game in single-player mode
Change DifficultyDifficulty Dropdown in ToolbarSelect across Easy, Medium, Hard, and Master AI engines to sharpen your tactical instincts
Touchscreen SnapSingle-finger tap with magnetic snapAuto-aligns touch coordinates to the nearest intersection for effortless mobile play

Essential Tactical Formations Quick Reference

  • Open Three (Live 3): A three-stone line open at both ends (e.g., _XXX_). If unblocked, it inevitably blossoms into an unstoppable Open Four on the subsequent turn.
  • Closed Four (Rush 4): A four-stone sequence blocked at one end or with an internal gap (e.g., OXXXX_). It carries absolute initiative, forcing an immediate, mandatory opponent response.
  • Double Attack Formations:
    • Double Three (3-3): A single stone creates two Open Threes simultaneously. The opponent can only block one side, handing you guaranteed victory.
    • Four-Three (4-3): The premier universal winning move: forces a block on the Four, followed by an unstoppable Open Four on the Three!

Master Heuristic: "Chase the Lights" Quick Reference

  1. Top-Down Sweep (Pass 1): For every cell in Row 1 that doesn't match the target state, click the button directly below it in Row 2. Continue cascading downward until Row 4, compressing all deviations into Row 5.

About Nonogram (Picross / Griddlers / Picture Logic)

Nonogram (also famously known as Picross, Griddlers, or Picture Logic) is an addictive picture puzzle game loved by players of all ages around the world. Imagine you are a detective uncovering a hidden mystery picture: numbers along the top and left edges tell you how many consecutive black blocks exist in each row and column. With 100% pure deductive logic and zero guessing, filling in the correct black pixels and placing crosses on empty spots will reveal an enchanting pixel artwork right under your fingers!

The Two Golden Rules of Clue Numbers

  • The number tells you the block length: If a row shows 5, it has 5 continuous filled black cells. If it shows 2 3, there is a block of 2, followed by a gap, then a block of 3.
  • Blocks must be separated by at least one space: Two black blocks can never touch directly; there must always be at least one empty square (cross) between them.
  • Completed clues turn grey: Once all blocks in a row or column are correctly placed, the numbers automatically dim and strike through to let you focus on remaining lines!

  • Trick 1: Push from Both Ends (Find the Overlap): If a row has 10 cells and a block of 8: push it all the way left (cells 1 to 8), then all the way right (cells 3 to 10). Notice that cells 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, and 8 are covered in both cases! Paint those 6 cells black immediately! Quick math: 10 - 8 = 2 empty cells. Block size 8 minus 2 empty cells equals 6 overlapping black cells!
  • Trick 2: Count from the Wall (Edge Pinning): If cell 1 at the edge is black, and the first clue is 4, count 4 cells straight from the edge and paint them black. Then place a cross (×) right after it!
  • Trick 3: Small Spaces Can't Fit Big Blocks: If you see a small gap of 2 empty cells between two crosses, but your shortest remaining block is 3, that small gap cannot hold anything. Cross out both cells right away!
  • Trick 4: Close the Doors When Done: When a block reaches its designated clue length (like 3 full black cells for a clue of 3), cap both ends with crosses so it doesn't accidentally grow too long.

Four Pillars of Deadlock Prevention

  1. Corner Deadlock: A crate pushed into a non-target 90° corner formed by walls can never be retrieved, immediately rendering the puzzle unsolvable.
  2. Wall Deadlock: A crate pushed flush against a flat wall loses one degree of freedom and can only travel along the wall. If the wall has no target or exit bay, it is permanently stranded.
  3. 2×2 Block Deadlock: Any 2×2 cluster of obstacles (walls and crates) completely locks all involved crates permanently.
  4. Inside-Out Packing Order: Always fill the innermost, deepest targets first! Seating an outer target prematurely will block the access tunnel for interior destinations.

Real-Time Multiplayer Speed PK

  • Identical Map Parity: Both contestants race on the exact same warehouse blueprint.
  • Live Progress HUD: Track your opponent's completion percentage (0%~100%), move count, and pacing in real time.
  • First to Complete Claims the Round: Master smooth pathfinding and forward planning to dominate the leaderboards.

Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ)

Is it possible to push two boxes if they are in a straight line?

No. The keeper can only push a single crate at a time. If two crates are aligned sequentially, the movement is blocked until you navigate around them and push one aside.

Where can I study the formal PSPACE-completeness proof and deadlock graph theory?

Explore our definitive masterclass monograph: 《Classic Sokoban Ultimate Guide & Graph Theory Pathfinding Masterbook》, featuring Culberson's complexity theorems, dead-square topological preprocessing, and reverse induction algorithms!

game.sudoku.seo_desc:
Quick Start & Sudoku Basic Rules

Sudoku is a globally beloved number-placement logic puzzle. The standard game is played on a 9×9 grid, partitioned into nine 3×3 subgrids (blocks). It requires zero mathematical calculations—only pure deductive reasoning. Your objective is to fill all empty cells with digits from 1 to 9, adhering strictly to three golden rules:

  • Each Row: Must contain digits 1 through 9 exactly once, without repetition.
  • Each Column: Must contain digits 1 through 9 exactly once, without repetition.
  • Each 3×3 Block: Must contain digits 1 through 9 exactly once, without repetition.

Complete Controls & Keyboard Shortcuts Guide

To deliver a seamless solving experience on desktop, tablet, and mobile, Puzzle PK provides full keyboard hotkeys and touch controls:

ActionKey / GestureDescription
Input NumberKeyboard 1 ~ 9 or Onscreen NumpadFill the selected cell with the chosen digit
Move Cursor↑ ↓ ← → or W A S DNavigate across the 9×9 grid without lifting your hands from the keyboard
Pencil NotesKeyboard Space or N / Toolbar ✏️ ButtonToggle draft notes mode to mark multiple candidate digits in tricky cells
Erase CellKeyboard Backspace / Delete or ⌫ EraserClear the filled digit or pencil marks in the selected cell
UndoKeyboard Z or ↩ Undo ButtonStep backwards to reverse recent placements or erasures
Reset BoardKeyboard R KeyClear all your input numbers and restart the current puzzle from scratch
TouchscreenTap cell to select, then tap bottom numpadFully responsive mobile and tablet layout for comfortable one-handed play

Built-in Assistant Tools & Solving Tips

  • Crosshair & Identical Number Highlight: Selecting any cell or entering a number immediately highlights all identical digits on the board alongside its intersecting row, column, and block—giving you instantaneous visual clarity.
  • Instant Conflict Detection: If you mistakenly enter a number that violates row, column, or block constraints, it will be highlighted in red so errors don't snowball.
  • Auto-Save Progress: Your single-player moves and elapsed timer are continuously saved locally. If you close the tab or reload, you can resume right where you left off.

Multiplayer PK Battle Modes

Craving an adrenaline-pumping mental showdown? Step into the multiplayer lobby to challenge friends or duel global players in real time:

  • Speed Mode (Speed PK): Every player in the room faces the identical high-difficulty puzzle. Race against time to deduce and input digits—the first player to submit a 100% correct solution wins!
  • Steal Mode (Steal PK): All players share a single shared board! Correctly placed digits earn points and claim territory; entering an incorrect number incurs a freeze penalty. Fast reflexes and ruthless strategy reign supreme!

Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ)

What should I do if I feel stuck with no obvious moves?

Sudoku puzzles never require guessing! When progress stalls, toggle on "Pencil Notes" to mark candidate numbers in tight cells, or scan lines with the fewest remaining empty spots. For in-depth methods like Naked Singles, Pointing Pairs, and the X-Wing theorem, check out the comprehensive guide below.

How do the difficulty levels differ?

Easy puzzles offer abundant starting clues for newcomers. Medium and Hard levels introduce intersecting exclusions, while Expert difficulty demands chaining theorems. Start with Easy to build confidence, aiming for 100% accuracy before focusing on speed.

game.tetris.seo_desc:
Classic Tetris Core Rules & Objectives

Tetris is the undisputed masterpiece of geometric spatial reasoning and reaction speed in video game history. Played on a standard 10×20 matrix (200 squares in total), seven iconic geometric shapes known as Tetrominoes fall continuously from the top. The rules of survival and mastery are crystal-clear:

  • Line Clear Mechanic: Guide falling tetrominoes horizontally and rotate them to form solid horizontal lines without any gaps. When a row of 10 cells is completely filled, it clears instantly and awards points. Up to 4 lines can be cleared simultaneously (Tetris);
  • Top Out Condition: As lines are cleared, gravity accelerates. If the stack of blocks reaches above the 20th row skyline where new pieces can no longer spawn, the game ends (Top Out);
  • Modern 7-Bag Randomizer: Governed by the official Tetris Guideline, tetrominoes are dealt from continuous randomized bags of 7 distinct pieces, completely eliminating endless piece droughts.

Official Guideline Standard Scoring Table

Puzzle PK strictly adheres to the international official Tetris Guideline standard scoring framework. Points scale proportionally with the current gravity speed level (Level):

Action / Clear Type Formula Level 1 Points Level 5 Points Mechanic & Competitive Impact
Single Clear 100 × Level 100 pts 500 pts Basic stack maintenance (1 line cleared)
Double Clear 300 × Level 300 pts 1,500 pts Clears 2 lines; sends 1 garbage line in PK
Triple Clear 500 × Level 500 pts 2,500 pts Clears 3 lines; sends 2 garbage lines in PK
Tetris Clear (4 Lines) 800 × Level 800 pts 4,000 pts I-piece strike; clears 4 lines; sends 4 garbage lines
Back-to-Back Tetris 1200 × Level (1.5×) 1,200 pts 6,000 pts Consecutive Tetris clears trigger a 1.5× score boost and +1 extra garbage line
All Clear (Perfect Clear) Bonus 2000 × Level +2,000 pts +10,000 pts Wiping the entire matrix clean yields a massive bonus and launches 10 garbage lines!
Combo Chain Bonus 50 × (Combo - 1) × Level 50 ~ 250+ pts 250 ~ 1,250+ pts Consecutive clears without interruption escalate rapid combo score bonuses
Soft Drop 1 pt / cell Per cell Per cell Hold Down key to glide faster; awards 1 pt per cell traversed
Hard Drop 2 pts / cell Per cell Per cell Press Space to instant drop; awards 2 pts per cell traversed

Controls & Gestures Reference Table

Puzzle PK provides responsive input mappings optimized for desktop keyboards and mobile touchscreens:

Action Desktop Keyboard Mobile Touch / Virtual Buttons Behavior & Physical Mechanics
Move Left ← or A Swipe Left (>25px) / Tap ◀ Shifts falling piece 1 column to the left; hold for continuous shifting
Move Right → or D Swipe Right (>25px) / Tap ▶ Shifts falling piece 1 column to the right; hold for continuous shifting
Rotate Clockwise ↑, W, or Z Quick Tap (<300ms) / Tap ↻ Rotates piece clockwise with SRS wall kicks against walls or overhangs
Soft Drop ↓ or S Swipe Down (>35px) / Tap ▼ Accelerates downward fall while retaining placement adjustment window
Hard Drop Space Fast Flick Down (>60px) / Tap ⚡ Instantly drops piece to bottom and locks it in 0ms; vital for speed sprinting
Hold Piece C or Shift Tap Hold Box in top-left corner Stores active piece into hold queue and swaps out held piece (once per piece)
Instant Restart R Tap 'Play Again' on game over modal Instantly clears matrix and restarts session in solo practice mode

Key Scoring Techniques & Attack Formations

  • Tetris Clear (4 Lines): Build a flat 9-column stack leaving a 1-wide open well along the side. Drop the cyan I-piece straight down to clear 4 lines at once for huge points;
  • T-Spin (TSD / TST): Rotate the purple T-piece into tight slots using SRS wall kick twists. T-Spin Double sends 4 garbage lines—matching a 4-line Tetris with half the blocks;
  • Back-to-Back (B2B): Clearing consecutive high-difficulty lines (Tetris or T-Spins without intervening single/double clears) awards a 1.5× score multiplier and extra garbage lines;
  • Combo Chains: Clearing lines with consecutive dropped pieces triggers escalating combo point bonuses and relentless attack pressure.

Multiplayer PK: Garbage Line Cancellation

Compete in real-time 1v1 PvP or arena battles with global puzzle masters:

  • Garbage Distribution: Single clears send 0; Double sends 1; Triple sends 2; Tetris sends 4; T-Spin Double sends 4; All Clear sends 10 devastating garbage lines!
  • 2.5s Incoming Threat Buffer: Incoming garbage doesn't immediately lift your board. It enters a 2.5-second warning buffer alert countdown;
  • Line Cancellation: Clear lines during the 2.5-second buffer to cancel incoming garbage 1-to-1, neutralizing rival attacks before they reach your stack;
  • Downstacking: Cleanly clear blocks covering garbage well holes to cut through messy stacks and trigger reverse counter-attack combos!

Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ)

Can I experience a long drought without receiving an I-piece?

No. Puzzle PK implements the standard 7-Bag randomizer. Each cycle of 7 pieces contains exactly one of each tetromino. The maximum possible gap between two I-pieces is 12 pieces.

What is a Wall Kick? Why does a stuck piece still rotate?

The Super Rotation System (SRS) tests a sequence of 5 offset positions when a rotation is initially blocked, shifting the piece 1 space left, right, or upward to squeeze it into tight crevices.

game.watersort.seo_desc:
Water Sort Puzzle Core Rules & Master Guide

Water Sort Puzzle is a mesmerizing brain teaser that merges discrete combinatorial graph theory, color-matching mechanics, and fluid physics aesthetics. Facing multiple test tubes filled with layered colored liquids, players execute precise topological transfers and batch consolidations until every tube contains only one pure color or is completely empty.

🎮 Controls & Keyboard Shortcuts

Control Mode Key / Gesture Function Description
Select Source Tube Click / Tap Elevates the tube and selects its top contiguous color stream
Pour to Target Click Target Tube Triggers pouring animation, batch-transferring fluid into the destination
Deselect Click Source Again Returns the tube to its resting position and clears selection
Instant Restart R Key / Restart Button Instantly resets the current board and moves counter in single player
Smart Hint Toolbar 💡 Hint Computes the optimal valid move; warns and recovers if state is locked
Difficulty Selector Top Dropdown Easy (7 Tubes / 5 Colors), Medium (11 / 9), Hard (16 / 14)

🧪 The Four Physical Pouring Axioms

  • Color Matching Axiom: You can ONLY pour fluid onto a target tube if its top layer matches the incoming color. Mismatched colors cannot contact each other.
  • Capacity Invariant: Every tube has a strict physical capacity of 4 units. Once a tube has 4 units, no additional liquid can enter.
  • Greedy Batch Pour Principle: All contiguous units of the top color are transferred in one single operation, up to the remaining capacity of the destination.
  • Empty Tube Buffer: The 2 empty buffer tubes provided at the start are the most precious degrees of freedom on the board and can accept any color.

🧠 Five Core Mental Heuristics

  1. Buffer Conservation Law: Empty tubes are strategic registers. Never park liquid into an empty tube without a clear derivation chain to free another tube.
  2. Top-Down Excavation: Identify foundational colors at tube bottoms and methodically peel away covering layers by merging them into matching destinations.
  3. Split Avoidance Principle: Never divide an already consolidated color stream (2 or 3 units) across multiple tubes; fragmentation causes deadlocks.
  4. Bottom-Up Foundation & Sealing: When a tube reaches 3 units of pure color at the base, prioritize sealing the 4th unit to permanently reduce problem complexity to N-1.
  5. Chained Cascade Maneuver: Utilize an empty buffer to execute cyclic transfers (A→Empty, B→A, C→B, Empty→C), accomplishing clean realignment while restoring the buffer.

⚔️ Multiplayer Speed PK Arena

  • Identical Seed Racing: All players receive the exact same initial tube configuration, guaranteeing 100% fair skill-based competition.
  • Live Telemetry HUD: Real-time progress bars show opponents' completion rates and move counts. Balance deliberate accuracy against raw speed.
  • Deadlock Recovery: Press R in single player to instantly restart; in PK mode, stay calm and reverse tangled transfers to recover the board.

👉 For the complete mathematical state-space analysis, IDA* solver proofs, deadlock taxonomy, and the Twelve-Word Formula, visit the Water Sort Master Strategy Monograph.

tutorial.block.clear_desc: Filling multiple rows or columns simultaneously triggers a combo for bonus points. Plan placements to maximise clears!
tutorial.block.end_desc: When none of the tray pieces can fit anywhere on the board, the game ends. Keep lines clear to preserve space!
tutorial.block.goal_desc: Place block pieces onto the grid to fill complete rows or columns. Clear lines to score — survive as long as possible!
tutorial.block.place_desc: Drag a piece from the tray at the bottom onto an empty area of the board. Invalid spots are highlighted in red.
tutorial.classic2048.end_desc: The game ends when the board is full and no more moves can be made in any direction.
tutorial.classic2048.goal_desc: Slide tiles on a 4x4 grid to combine them and reach the 2048 tile!
tutorial.classic2048.merge_desc: Two tiles with the same number merge into one (2+2=4, 4+4=8...). A new 2 or 4 appears on an empty spot.
tutorial.classic2048.slide_desc: Use arrow keys or swipe the screen (Up, Down, Left, Right) to move all tiles in that direction.
tutorial.codebreaker.feedback_desc: 🟢 Green = correct digit in the right position. 🟡 Yellow = correct digit in the wrong position. ⚫ Grey = digit not in the code.
tutorial.codebreaker.goal_desc: Guess the secret code within the allowed number of attempts. Each guess reveals clues about your accuracy.
tutorial.codebreaker.hint_desc: Stuck? Tap 💡 to reveal one correct digit in its exact position. Use hints wisely!
tutorial.codebreaker.strategy_desc: Start with digits that cover many possibilities. Use the clues from each guess to eliminate options.
tutorial.connect.cross_desc: Lines will break if they cross or overlap each other.
tutorial.connect.draw_desc: Drag from one color dot to its matching pair to draw a pipe.
tutorial.connect.fill_desc: You must cover every single empty square on the board to complete the puzzle.
tutorial.connect.goal_desc: Pair all matching colors on the board with a continuous line.
tutorial.drop2048.drop_desc: Tap or click a column to drop the current ball there. A preview line shows exactly where it will land.
tutorial.drop2048.end_desc: The game ends when a column is full and the next ball can't be placed. Watch column heights and spread your drops evenly.
tutorial.drop2048.goal_desc: Drop numbered balls and merge matching ones to double their value. Chain merges to reach 2048 and beyond for the highest score!
tutorial.drop2048.merge_desc: When two balls with the same number touch they merge instantly: 2+2→4, 4+4→8… all the way to 2048!
tutorial.gomoku.ai_desc: In single-player mode choose Easy, Medium, or Hard AI. Hard AI plans several moves ahead — start with Easy to practice!
tutorial.gomoku.defense_desc: Block your opponent's four-in-a-row immediately. Look for double-three or double-four threats to force a win.
tutorial.gomoku.goal_desc: Be the first to connect five stones in a row — horizontally, vertically, or diagonally.
tutorial.gomoku.turn_desc: Players alternate placing one stone per turn on any empty intersection. Black moves first.
tutorial.hashi.bridge_desc: Click two adjacent islands (horizontally or vertically) to build a bridge. Click again for a double bridge, and a third time to remove.
tutorial.hashi.cross_desc: Bridges cannot cross each other or pass through islands. All islands must be connected.
tutorial.hashi.goal_desc: Use bridges to connect all islands. The number on each island indicates how many bridges are connected to it.
tutorial.hexa.clear_desc: Clearing multiple lines at once triggers a combo for multiplied points. The more you clear together, the bigger the reward!
tutorial.hexa.end_desc: The game ends when none of the three tray pieces can fit anywhere on the board. Manage your space wisely!
tutorial.hexa.goal_desc: Place hexagonal pieces on the board. Fill complete rows or diagonals to clear them and score points.
tutorial.hexa.place_desc: Drag a piece from the tray at the bottom and drop it onto the board. A preview highlights where it will land.
tutorial.idiom.fill_desc: See an idiom with blanks and tap the correct characters from the keyboard
tutorial.idiom.goal_desc: Learn Chinese idioms through fill-in-blank and daily Wordle challenges
tutorial.idiom.story_desc: After each answer, discover the story and origin of the idiom
tutorial.idiom.wordle_desc: All players guess the same idiom each day. Green=correct, Yellow=present, Gray=absent
tutorial.lightsout.goal_desc: Supports dual modes: [All Lit] and [All Out] (toggle anytime at the top, default All Lit). Click tiles to flip orthogonal neighbors and clear the board!
tutorial.lightsout.hint_desc: Stuck? Tap 💡 to highlight the next recommended cell to click and get back on track.
tutorial.lightsout.logic_desc: Every puzzle has an exact solution where each cell is clicked at most once. Extra clicks just undo your progress.
tutorial.lightsout.toggle_desc: Clicking a light toggles it AND its four orthogonal neighbours simultaneously. This is the core mechanic!
tutorial.math24.goal_desc: Use all four numbers on the card with any combination of + − × ÷ to make exactly 24.
tutorial.math24.ops_desc: You can use addition, subtraction, multiplication, and division. Parentheses are applied automatically.
tutorial.math24.select_desc: Tap a number, then tap an operator, then tap another number. Keep combining until you reach 24!
tutorial.math24.timer_desc: Solve as fast as possible to earn maximum stars and XP. Can't solve it? Try Shuffle for a new puzzle.
tutorial.mine.flag_desc: Right-click (or long-press) to place a flag on a suspected mine. Flags prevent accidental reveals.
tutorial.mine.goal_desc: Reveal all safe cells without hitting any mines. The numbers tell you how many mines are adjacent.
tutorial.mine.hint_desc: Stuck? Tap the 💡 Hint button — it safely reveals one guaranteed-safe cell for you.
tutorial.mine.numbers_desc: A number shows how many mines touch that cell. Use them to deduce which cells are safe and which are mines.
tutorial.mine.reveal_desc: Left-click (or tap) a cell to reveal it. The first click is always safe — a blank area will open up.
tutorial.nonogram.cross_desc: Toggle mode to cross out cells that must be empty.
tutorial.nonogram.fill_desc: Click a cell to fill it.
tutorial.nonogram.goal_desc: Fill cells based on hints to reveal the picture.
tutorial.nonogram.hints_desc: Numbers indicate consecutive filled cells in that row/col.
tutorial.sliding.goal_desc: Arrange the numbered tiles in order from top-left to bottom-right, leaving the blank space at the end.
tutorial.sliding.hint_desc: Stuck? Tap 💡 to get a recommended move and find the right direction.
tutorial.sliding.move_desc: Tap any tile adjacent to the blank space to slide it in. Only tiles directly next to the gap can move.
tutorial.sliding.strategy_desc: Solve the puzzle row by row from the top. Avoid disturbing rows you've already completed while working on lower ones.
tutorial.sokoban.controls_desc: Swipe or tap the directional arrows to move the character. On desktop you can also use arrow keys or WASD.
tutorial.sokoban.goal_desc: Push all the boxes (📦) onto the target spots (★). When a box lands on a target it turns dark.
tutorial.sokoban.rules_desc: Boxes can be pushed but not pulled. Plan ahead — pushing a box into a corner with no target is a dead end!
tutorial.sokoban.undo_desc: Tap ↩ to undo your last move. Tap 💡 for a hint. Both are limited per puzzle, so use them wisely.
tutorial.sudoku.goal_desc: Fill a 9×9 grid so every row, column, and 3×3 box contains the digits 1–9 exactly once.
tutorial.sudoku.hint_desc: Tap 💡 Hint to reveal one correct digit. Hints use a limited pool — use them wisely!
tutorial.sudoku.notes_desc: Enable Notes mode to jot down possible digits in a cell without committing. Great for narrowing down candidates.
tutorial.sudoku.rules_desc: No digit can repeat in the same row, column, or 3×3 box. Tap a cell and then tap a number to fill it in.
tutorial.tetris.controls_desc: Swipe left/right to move, swipe up or tap to rotate, swipe down to speed up, double-tap to drop. On desktop use arrow keys.
tutorial.tetris.goal_desc: Stack falling pieces to complete full rows — completed rows clear automatically and earn you points. Don't let pieces reach the top!
tutorial.tetris.scoring_desc: Clear multiple rows at once for a massive bonus: 2 rows ×3, 3 rows ×5, 4 rows (Tetris!) ×8.
tutorial.tetris.strategy_desc: Keep your stack flat and fill holes early. Save I-pieces for Tetris clears to maximise your score.
tutorial.watersort.goal_desc: Sort all the colored liquids so each tube contains only one color. All tubes must be pure!
tutorial.watersort.hint_desc: Tap 💡 to see the next recommended pour. Great for when you feel stuck!
tutorial.watersort.rules_desc: You can only pour onto a matching color or into an empty tube. You can't pour if the destination is full.
tutorial.watersort.select_desc: Tap a tube to select it (it will lift up), then tap another tube to pour the top color into it.
